answer: Graders can be tested with hidden canaries. Auditors slip answers whose fair score is already settled into the queue, some quietly broken and some excellent, like weeds planted on purpose in a garden bed. No grader can tell a canary from a live seat, so each account must truly read what it scores; one that rubber-stamps or copies a sibling's marks drifts from the known scores and loses standing. A farm of fifty fakes must pay for fifty full readings, and shared marks sink together like stones in a river, so its margin stays an ember, never a fire.
